result.title: TRACK: Tool-Augmented Reasoning over Time Series for Fault Diagnosis in Power Management System
result.summary: Fault diagnosis in power management systems running multiple loads relies on experts manually inspecting current and voltage waveforms, which fails to scale across deployed units. We present TRACK, which pairs a time series encoder with a Small Language Model to produce structured, physics-grounded diagnostic reports, calling tools for exact, verifiable calculations. It operates on-device, keeping proprietary sensor data local and avoiding expensive API calls. We introduce a rubric-based framework that evaluates these reports by scoring structure, signal fidelity, physics reasoning, diagnosis, and actionability through per-criterion verdicts. On a 15-class multi-load simulated benchmark, TRACK achieves over 95% fault-category accuracy and generalizes to out-of-distribution faults, whereas the best encoder-probing baseline reaches only 58% accuracy.

AI.brief_summary: TRACK 将时间序列编码器与小语言模型结合，用于电力管理系统多负载故障诊断：通过调用工具完成精确可核验的计算，生成结构化、具物理依据的诊断报告，并提出按结构、信号保真度、物理推理、诊断与可行动性逐项给出判定的 rubric 评估框架。
AI.relevance_reason: 「调用外部工具做可核验计算」以及 rubric 中将「信号保真」与「物理推理」「诊断」分开打分的做法，可能可供核查 LVR/VLM 中推理是否真正使用模态证据及贡献分配的评价方式；但该工作属时序故障诊断应用，与视觉 latent 推理无直接联系，迁移性需较多核查。
